prompt: A finished graphic design poster, seen flat-on and full bleed; the image is the poster itself, not a mockup on a wall. Keep the finish of the reference posters, but not their primary palette. Ground: one flat solid field of flour-cream paper. A single thick transit-map line of one fixed width, in burnt rust orange, enters from the top edge, bends only at 90 and 45 degrees with one consistent corner radius, and zigzags down the whole sheet to leave through the bottom edge. Along it sit four large station dots, white with thick charcoal rings, and beside each station, in order from top to bottom, one word in bold heavy charcoal sans-serif: "BAKERY", "HOSPITAL", "MARKET", "PRINT WORKS". At each station, a small flat isometric building sits right on the line, hard-edged, its walls in sage green with charcoal solid shadow planes: a bakery with a chimney, a hospital block, a market hall with a pitched roof, a print works with a saw-tooth roof; true isometric at 30 degrees, verticals vertical, no vanishing point. The headline "NIGHT SHIFT LINE" is built as a long solid sage green block lettered in huge charcoal capitals on its face, and the rust line runs straight through a gap cut in that block, so the headline is a viaduct the line passes under. Small, under the headline: "N4 · ALL NIGHT". Inks, four only: burnt rust orange, sage green, charcoal, and a pale blush pink used only for the lit windows of the four buildings. The only words are "NIGHT SHIFT LINE", "BAKERY", "HOSPITAL", "MARKET", "PRINT WORKS" and "N4 · ALL NIGHT", spelled exactly. No people except at most one tiny geometric figure at the bakery door. No gradients, no glow, no gloss, no soft shadows, no other text, no small print, no logos.

Background above the tram roof: flat solid ochre gold ink. No perspective, no gradients, no glow, no reflections in the glass, no gloss, no soft shadows, no other text, no small print, no logos.

The inside of the O's doorway is a solid navy void. One tiny geometric figure, built from an ochre circle and a coral rectangle, stands on the rails just outside the O, under one-sixth of the image height and much smaller, to show the scale of the letters. The only words are "OWL", "NIGHT LINE N4" and "EVERY NIGHT", spelled exactly. Asymmetric layout: the letters sit in the upper two-thirds, the L partly cropped by the right edge.
